name: UCI Wine Quality — red and white samples
description: All 6,497 real red/white vinho verde wine samples from UCI Wine Quality. One row per source observation. Source values are preserved in a separate baseline table; this dataset queries a labelled working copy restored after the data-change demo.
licence_note: CC BY 4.0. Cortez, P., Cerdeira, A., Almeida, F., Matos, T., & Reis, J. (2009). Wine Quality [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.24432/C56S3T. Added wine_type and stable source-row IDs; a quality score is temporarily changed only in the labelled demo working copy, then restored.
empty_message: No matching wine samples were found for these filters.

sample_count.label: Wine sample count
sample_count.description: Number of source observations, not unique brands or people

average_quality.label: Average quality score
average_quality.description: Arithmetic mean of sensory quality scores on a 0–10 scale

average_alcohol.label: Average alcohol (% by volume)
average_alcohol.description: Mean alcohol content, percent by volume

planning_notes: Count wines/samples -> sample_count; average quality -> average_quality; average alcohol -> average_alcohol; average residual sugar -> average_residual_sugar. High-quality means our explicit analysis threshold quality >= 7, not a separate source category. Filter wine_type with RED or WHITE, quality with integers. Never invent sales, revenue, dates, customers, country, wine brands or grape types. Example 'How many wine samples have a quality score of at least 7?': {"status":"query","message":"Count samples with quality at least 7.","metrics":["sample_count"],"dimensions":[],"filters":[{"field":"quality","operator":"gte","values":[7]}],"sort":[],"limit":20}.
limitations: Real historical Portuguese vinho verde measurements; do not generalize these results to all wines.
High-quality (score >= 7) is our analysis convention, not a binary label supplied by UCI.
No timestamps, brand, grape variety, selling price, customer or causal information is provided.
All original measurements are loaded; this API currently exposes four aggregate metrics and wine-type/quality grouping and filters.
Questions execute against a labelled working copy. The demo temporarily changes one score from 6 to 7, then restores it. Source table and downloaded archive are never edited by the demo.
Multi-step support is bounded to two scalar scopes, subset shares, and groups above the row-weighted population average; arbitrary chains and conversational follow-ups are unsupported.

analysis_examples.question: Compare average alcohol of red wines against white wines.
